I would keep the farm simple, practical, and yield-focused. In Quzhou County, the standard and most reliable system for me is a winter wheat plus summer maize rotation, because it matches the local climate, irrigation conditions, machinery use, and market habits. Since I have a university education, I would lean on improved seed, measured fertilizer use, and tighter field management rather than trying to spread risk across many small specialty crops. At the start of the growing season, my main work would be managing the standing winter wheat through spring water and fertilizer, disease and pest control, and then turning the land quickly into summer maize after wheat harvest. I would use improved or hybrid seed where the yield advantage is clear, keep tillage moderate with rotary preparation after harvest to save time, and avoid excessive chemical use by aiming for necessary sprays rather than routine over-application. My goal would be stable output, manageable labor, and efficient use of water and fertilizer on a wheat-maize double-cropping system.
